chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn 'Isa from Hariz said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (or Mufrad, contextually implying the Hajj ritual) who missed both standings (at Arafat and Muzdalifah). He said to him: [Wait] until the sunrise of the Day of Nahr (Eid al-Adha). If the sun rises on the Day of Nahr, then he has not performed Hajj, and he makes it a single Umrah, and upon him is the Hajj next year.

key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَانِ: The two essential standings (at Arafat and Muzdalifah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim misses both the standing at Arafat and Muzdalifah?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the specific timing for the 'Standing at Mawqif' (Wuquf) at Mashar al-Haram; if a pilgrim misses both essential stands until after sunrise on Eid al-Adha, their Hajj is invalidated. Consequently, the rituals performed are downgraded to a single Umrah, and the pilgrim incurs the obligation of Qada (making up) the Hajj in the following year, highlighting the strict adherence to temporal conditions in Shia jurisprudence.
